2027-05-05.title: Wednesday of the Sixth Week of Easter
readings: What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you
Heaven and earth are full of your glory (or: Alleluia)
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth
2027-05-05.alt: Easter weekday of the sixth week (Year I). The Alleluia is sung before the Gospel, the paschal candle burns beside the ambo, and the Regina Caeli takes the place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The Church is now turning towards the Ascension and the coming of the Holy Spirit. Liturgical colour: white. Tomorrow, in India, is an Easter weekday; the Ascension is kept on Sunday 9 May.
2027-05-05.verse: When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth; for he will not speak on his own, but will speak whatever he hears, and he will declare to you the things that are to come.
theo: Paul has been hurried out of Thessalonica and Beroea and brought, almost alone, to Athens, the most famous city of learning in the ancient world. Walking its streets, he sees temples, statues and altars everywhere. He is invited to speak at the Areopagus, the hill and council where the city's philosophers and judges met. His speech is a model of how to speak of Christ to people of another culture. He does not begin with insults; he begins with respect: “Athenians, I see how extremely religious you are in every way.” He has noticed an altar “To an unknown god,” and he builds on it: “What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you.” Then he speaks of the Creator who “made the world and everything in it,” who does not live in shrines made by hands, who gives to all “life and breath and all things,” and who made all nations from one ancestor, “so that they would search for God and perhaps grope for him and find him, though indeed he is not far from each one of us.” He even quotes their own poets: “In him we live and move and have our being,” and “For we too are his offspring.” Only at the end does he name what is new: God has fixed a day of judgment “by a man whom he has appointed, and of this he has given assurance to all by raising him from the dead.”

At the word “resurrection” the meeting breaks up. “When they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some scoffed; but others said, ‘We will hear you again about this.’” It looks like a failure, and Paul soon leaves for Corinth. Yet Luke adds: “some of them joined him and became believers, including Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.” Seeds are sown even where the harvest is small. The Psalm calls the whole creation to praise, “kings of the earth and all peoples,” “young men and women alike, old and young together,” for the Lord's “glory is above earth and heaven.” In the Gospel Jesus explains why the Church's understanding of him can grow without changing: “I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.” The Spirit does not bring a new Gospel; “he will take what is mine and declare it to you.” He leads the Church deeper into the one truth that is Christ. That is what Paul did at Athens: he found in the Greeks' own searching a door for the truth of Christ. The Second Vatican Council teaches that the Church rejects nothing that is true and holy in other religions, while she proclaims without ceasing Christ, “the way, and the truth, and the life” (Nostra Aetate 2). In a land of many temples and many seekers like India, Paul at the Areopagus is a teacher for us: respectful, clear, and unashamed of the Resurrection.

Paul begins with respect and with the Creator.

live: Notice today one good thing in a friend or colleague of another faith: their prayerfulness, honesty or generosity. Thank God for it.
Before reading the Bible or the Catechism today, pray: Come, Spirit of truth, guide me into the truth of Jesus.
2027-05-05.prayer: God our Creator, in you we live and move and have our being, and you are not far from each one of us. You let the peoples of the earth search for you and grope for you; reveal to them your Son, whom you raised from the dead. Give us the respect, clarity and courage of St Paul at Athens. Send us the Spirit of truth, who takes what belongs to Jesus and declares it to us, so that we may be led into all the truth and praise you with all creation. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Athenians worshipped an unknown god. At the altar the God who is “not far from each one of us” comes closer still: in the Eucharist the risen Christ is truly present, so that we who live and move and have our being in God may also receive God into ourselves.

quick: At the Areopagus in Athens Paul began from the altar “To an unknown god” and proclaimed the Creator, in whom we live and move and have our being.
When he spoke of the resurrection, some scoffed, but Dionysius, Damaris and others believed.
Jesus promises that the Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all the truth.
2027-05-05.action: Pray today for one friend of another faith by name, and treat them with the respect Paul showed the Athenians.
2027-05-05.question: Do I speak of my faith with both respect for others and courage about the Resurrection?

family.explain: Paul visited Athens, a city full of temples and statues. He saw an altar that said: To an unknown god. Paul said: I will tell you about this God! He made the world, he gives us life and breath, and he is very close to each of us. Then Paul told them about Jesus, who rose from the dead. Some laughed, but some believed.
family.intention: We pray for our neighbours and friends of other religions, that we may live together in peace and respect.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show our friends of other faiths that Jesus loves them?”

illus: Robert de Nobili, an Italian Jesuit who came to Madurai in 1606, saw that people kept their distance from the Gospel because it seemed foreign. He learned Tamil and Sanskrit, studied the Indian scriptures, dressed and lived simply as a sannyasi, and spoke of Christ in words his hearers could understand. Some of his methods were debated in his own day and were examined in Rome, which in 1623 allowed them with conditions. Like Paul at the Areopagus, he looked for the doors already present in a culture's search for God, and walked through them with the name of Jesus.

pm.open: Spirit of truth, guide us into all the truth, and teach us to speak of Jesus with respect and courage. Amen.
share: I see how extremely religious you are in every way (Acts 17:22). How do I look at people of other faiths?
He is not far from each one of us (Acts 17:27). When did I last feel how close God is?
He will guide you into all the truth (John 16:13). What truth of faith do I want the Holy Spirit to make clearer to me?
pm.resp: Heaven and earth are full of your glory.
interc: For dialogue between Christians and people of other religions in India, that it may grow in truth and friendship.
For teachers, scholars and students in universities, that they may search for God and find him.
For those who scoff at the Resurrection, that one day they may say, we will hear you again about this.
For catechists and preachers, that the Spirit of truth may guide their words.
For our group, that we may be ready to give an account of the hope that is in us.
pm.close: Father, in you we live and move and have our being. Send the Spirit of truth to guide your Church, and make us witnesses of the risen Christ to every people. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, imagine Paul in Athens: a Jewish tentmaker standing before the philosophers of the most learned city in the world. What does he say? He does not mock them. He says: Athenians, I see how extremely religious you are in every way (Acts 17:22). He has seen an altar to an unknown god, and he says: what you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you.

Paul shows us how to speak about Jesus to people of other faiths. First, respect. Look for the good that is already there, the search for God, the prayer, the longing. Second, start from what we share: the one Creator who gives life and breath to all, who made every nation, in whom we live and move and have our being (Acts 17:28). God is not far from each one of us.

Third, do not hide what is new. Paul ends with the Resurrection: God has raised Jesus from the dead. And some laughed. Some said: we will hear you again. Most went away. But Dionysius and a woman named Damaris and others believed. We do not measure success by the size of the crowd. Seeds sown in Athens grew into a Church.

In the Gospel Jesus says: when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth (John 16:13). The Spirit does not give a different Gospel; he takes what belongs to Jesus and makes it clearer. In our country of many temples and many seekers, let us ask the Spirit to give us Paul's respect and Paul's courage, and to guide us, and our neighbours, into the whole truth of the risen Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, Paul went to a big city called Athens, full of statues of gods. He saw an altar that said: to an unknown god. Paul said: I know this God! He made everything, he gives you life, and he is very close to you. His Son Jesus rose from the dead. When we talk to friends who do not know Jesus, let us be kind and polite like Paul, and tell them how good God is.

intro: Theme: “He will guide you into all the truth.”

concl: At Athens Paul showed how to proclaim Christ with respect for the search of others and without hiding the Resurrection.
The Spirit of truth continues that work in the Church, leading us and every people deeper into the one truth that is Christ.
2027-05-05.resolve: Pray each day until Pentecost: Come, Spirit of truth, and guide me and my neighbours into all the truth.
